outcome: maternal complications (bleeding, hysterectomies, intestinal/urinary surgical complications)
cohort: The study analyzed 13,841 deliveries, identifying 25 cases of placenta praevia and 17 cases of PAS at the County Emergency Clinical Hospital 'Saint Andrew the Apostle', Constanta, from 2018 to 2022.
finding: Smoking, uterine scars, and uterine fibroids are significant risk factors for placenta praevia with pathological adhesion, and ultrasound and MRI are highly accurate in diagnosing PAS.
mod_finding: Previous caesarean sections were a significant risk factor for PAS, accounting for 94.1% of cases, and caesarean section followed by hysterectomy was the preferred surgical approach.
